current_norm_sources: Gramota.ru current Rules / Full Academic Guide
Gramota.ru school theoretical course where morphology/form formation is required

audit_principle: FIPI task or codifier labels are not counted as identities. A school reopen candidate exists only when the official FIPI school content requires a productive orthographic decision with no active semantic owner in the 179. Broad exam analysis routes remain composites. Current normative confirmation is required before admission.

fipi_evidence: OGE 2026 orthography content explicitly includes invariable prefixes
EGE task 10 is spelling of hard/soft signs, prefixes and Ы/И after prefixes; FIPI task-10 notes include prefix and prefix-like material
confirmed_reopen_candidates.gap_reason: The 179 contain Z/S prefixes, PRE/PRI, separating signs, I/Y after prefixes and lexical boundaries, but no base owner for the stable spelling of ordinary invariant prefixes and the morphemic-vs-root/pseudo-prefix boundary.
confirmed_reopen_candidates.current_norm: Current academic/school descriptions preserve stable prefix spelling under the morphemic principle; e.g. consonants in в-, над-, об-, от-, под-, с- are not changed by pronunciation, while Z/S prefixes are routed to their separate rule.

fipi_evidence: EGE task 11 official 2026 navigator explicitly lists stable noun/adjective suffix spellings and several suffix families beyond the already materialized contrast pairs
OGE 2026 orthography includes suffix spelling across parts of speech
confirmed_reopen_candidates.gap_reason: Existing 179 own several productive suffix contrasts (-ЕК/-ИК, -ЧИК/-ЩИК, adjective suffix families, etc.) but lack the general route for an unstressed suffix vowel established by a stressed same-suffix form or a fixed conventional suffix pattern/dictionary fallback.
confirmed_reopen_candidates.current_norm: Full Academic Guide §42 states the general verification principle for unstressed suffix vowels and enumerates stable suffix spellings; current school rules separately list conventional noun/adjective suffix patterns.

fipi_evidence: EGE 2026 task 11 navigator explicitly: vowel in infinitive and past-tense verb form, examples ненавидеть, таяли, обессилеть/обессилить
OGE 2026 suffix content explicitly includes the vowel before -л- in the past-tense verb form
confirmed_reopen_candidates.gap_reason: The existing verb-suffix engine owns -ОВА/-ЕВА/-ЫВА/-ИВА and stressed -ВА-, while participle suffix engines own present/passive suffix choices. No active owner preserves/selects the infinitive stem vowel before -Л-, -ВШ-, -В, -ВШИ and related lexical -ЕТЬ/-ИТЬ contrasts.
confirmed_reopen_candidates.current_norm: Current Gramota rule groups vowels before past-form suffixes -л-, -вш-, -в, -вши: the infinitive stem vowel is preserved; current rule also confirms semantic/lexical contrasts such as обессилеть/обессилить and their derived forms.

fipi_evidence: OGE 2026 orthography explicitly includes vowels in gerund suffixes
EGE task 12 official route includes participle/gerund suffixes
confirmed_reopen_candidates.gap_reason: Existing 179 own gerund punctuation and НЕ with gerunds, but no orthographic/form-building owner for choosing standard gerund suffix patterns.
confirmed_reopen_candidates.current_norm: Current school grammar: imperfective gerunds use -а(-я) from the present stem where formation is possible; perfective gerunds normally use -в/-вши after vowel stems and -ши after consonant stems, with source-established variant/special forms.

confirmed_reopen_candidates.fipi_evidence: OGE 2026 orthography explicitly includes spelling of unstressed noun case endings.
confirmed_reopen_candidates.gap_reason: Wave B materialized difficult/special noun-ending families, but the 179 do not contain the ordinary productive base: determine declension/case/number or verify with the same inflectional type to choose the unstressed ending.
confirmed_reopen_candidates.current_norm: Current Full Academic Guide §67 and Gramota school rule explicitly define verification and declension patterns for unstressed noun endings.
confirmed_reopen_candidates.ownership_boundary: Existing special identities for -ИЙ/-ИЕ/-ИЯ/-ЬЕ, genitive plural, proper-name instrumental and special suffix/gender endings remain separate branches/families because they require additional classification or lexical control beyond the ordinary base rule.

confirmed_reopen_candidates.fipi_evidence: OGE 2026 orthography explicitly includes spelling norms for numeral endings; OGE/EGE language-norm routes also depend on normative numeral forms.
confirmed_reopen_candidates.gap_reason: The 179 contain special numeral paradigms (40/90/100; both components of 50–80/200–900) and a separate orthographic solid/separate/internal-sign engine, but no base inflection owner for numeral case endings as a class, including ordinary and special paradigms.
confirmed_reopen_candidates.current_norm: Current academic §67 and Gramota numeral grammar provide the general/special case paradigms, including 11–20/30, -десят, -сот, 40/90/100, полтора and related forms.
confirmed_reopen_candidates.ownership_boundary: Existing special numeral paradigm identities remain separately counted as difficult structured branches; this base owns the ordinary route and routing to those specials, not their full exception mastery.

scope_expansion_without_count.reason: OGE 2026 explicitly includes participle endings. Participles decline by the adjective-type case/number/gender mechanism; this is the same ending-selection operation, not a new independent orthographic identity.

scope_expansion_without_count.new_scope: include adverbial suffix/ending branches where the current rule applies
scope_expansion_without_count.reason: OGE includes O/E after sibilants in adverbs; the active source rule already owns O/E after sibilants in suffix/ending position, so this is a POS scope clarification, not a new decision.

exam_topics_checked_and_not_reopened: root vowels and consonants — existing root engines; note EGE 2026 explicitly says root consonants are not tested in the current task-9 material
Z/S, PRE/PRI, I/Y after prefixes, hard/soft signs — existing owners
productive noun/adjective/verb/participle suffix contrasts — existing owners, with the general fixed-suffix route added above
adjective endings — existing owner; participles scope-expanded above
N/NN — existing denominal and participle/verbal-adjective owners plus derived-adverb inheritance
compound and abbreviated words — existing compound/abbreviation systems
all FIPI punctuation families — already owned or composite across the punctuation identities created in Waves E–G
